scope_note: Independent visual review of receipts only. No integration, manifest, research or power changes. For each of the 5 requested slugs I viewed the native 1254px PNG, a 200px thumbnail, and targeted native crops (hoods/faces/eyes, hands and fingers, feet/toes/spurs, attributes such as the copper plate and the neck key, silkworms and rice origins, background figures and objects for pseudo-text), then compared them with the receipt visual_requirements and the research claims embedded in the ledger. Before writing, each PNG's SHA-256 was recomputed and matched against the receipt native_sha256, the Codex visual_review hash, the ledger item hash and the Codex root native review in drafts/root/codex-native-reviews.json. Claude wrote only root_visual_review (plus correction_notes on the rejects) and the receipt status, and synced the ledger item status. The ledger was re-read immediately before writing, and only the item status changed. No PNG, Codex visual_review, Codex native review or other receipt was modified. Rejects: nootaikok (a void-faced friar-robe-and-gloves Grim Reaper/Ringwraith silhouette makes the friendly benevolent spirit read as sinister, and the hunters read as European trappers, not Inuit); ogetsuhime (an ordinary photographic woman asleep on soil with motionless rice, calm at 200px, and maggot-like larvae scattered on a corpse instead of silkworms born from her head, which is macabre for a living-Shinto goddess).

results.reason: Viewed native 1254px, 200px, and hood, both-hand and hunter crops. What works: one figure dressed entirely in black (nootaikok-c03), legs hidden by the robe, with two black-gloved hands; the guiding hand shows a thumb and four fingers. It is in the water inside a still blue ice channel (c01/c03), guiding three seals toward hunters at the ice edge (c01/c04). No ice magic, aura or text. It fails for two reasons. (1) The hood is an empty black void with no face at all, on a European friar-style robe with flared sleeves and black leather gloves. That is the stock Grim Reaper/Ringwraith/Dementor silhouette, an icon of death and dread, and it turns the documented 'beneficial, friendly spirit' (c03; disposition benevolent, c01) into something sinister. At 200px it reads as a reaper reaching after the seals, not a benevolent spirit offering them. Under §6.5, a benevolent being must stay awe-inspiring and must not be made evil. (2) The three hunters read as bearded European/Siberian trappers in knitted caps and belted coats, not Inuit hunters, so the scene loses the Inuit tradition it illustrates. It fails the tradition-character check and Uji Sangar #7, because it shows the wrong character.
results.correction_notes: Keep: one spirit dressed in black (nootaikok-c03), in the water inside an iceberg/glacier (c01/c03), guiding seals toward hunters (c01/c03/c04). Keep the ice walls still, with no ice magic or breaking, and no aura or glow. Fix: (a) No void hood. Show a calm, dignified humanlike face, partly shadowed but clearly present, with two eyes and a benevolent expression turned toward the seals or the viewer, so it reads as a friendly guardian spirit. Make the black clothing a heavy hooded Arctic garment of black skin or fur (editorial), not a European friar's robe with flared sleeves and leather gloves. Nothing should read as the Grim Reaper, a Ringwraith or a Dementor. (b) If hunters are shown, they must read as Inuit hunters: fur-ruffed skin parkas and a harpoon, perhaps a kayak at the floe edge. Not bearded European trappers in knitted caps and belted coats. Keep them small and secondary. (c) Keep the majesty: the spirit large and close in the frame, a sweeping offering gesture, seals streaming past it toward the light, and one shaft of daylight through the ice falling on its face. No text.

results.reason: Viewed native 1254px, 200px, and slapping-hand, reaching-hand, face, feet and background-shelf crops. One humanlike yokai (nyubachi-bo-c02) with one head and one deeply lined, grimacing face. It has two eyes (the left one shadowed under the brim) and crooked ordinary teeth, with no horns or fangs. A broad hammered copper percussion plate sits tilted on its head (c01/c02/c06), with a raised central boss, a verdigris rim and dents. The boss and the gongs racked behind make it read as a cymbal, not a straw hat. Two arms: the raised hand slaps the plate side-on, with four fingers visible and the thumb under the palm, and patina flakes and dust burst off the metal. The other hand lunges at the viewer, thumb plus four fingers. Two legs in cloth foot-wraps, one planted forward and one behind. The ragged dark robe is fully opaque. The setting is a dark wooden theatre backstage with percussion storage (a stage instrument, c03/c06), lit by one amber lamp. The startling-noise action follows the Heisei-era explanation (c04, modern popular culture), which the receipt labels as later. It is shown only as a physical slap, with no sound rings or aura. The low lunge, the clawing hand and the grimace under the cymbal make it an uncanny instrument-yokai attacking, strong at 200px, not an ordinary man in a hat. Hyotan-kozo is left out by choice. No text; original design.

Viewed native 1254px, 200px, and face/eye, silkworm/hair and both-hand crops. What works: one adult goddess (ogetsuhime-c01) lying dead (c04) with her eyes closed, no wounds or blood, in a fully opaque ivory robe. Both hands show normal fingers. Rice rises from both closed eyes (c05), one sheaf from the left eye and one from the inner corner of the right, and white silkworms lie in her hair (c05). No Susanoo, aura or text. It fails the sangar test and the tone required for a living religion. (1) The figure is a photographic, ordinary young woman asleep on bare soil in a plain robe, and everything is still: the rice stands motionless, with no sign of growth erupting. At 200px it reads as a sleeping woman with a sheaf of rice over her face, calm rather than awe-inspiring. It fails Uji Sangar #2, #3 and #7 (ordinary woman, calm, static). (2) About a dozen segmented white larvae with dark heads are scattered across her hair and crawl onto the soil away from her head. On a corpse they read as maggots, a sign of decay, not as silkworms being born from her head. For a Kojiki deity of a living Shinto tradition, §6.5 asks for majesty, not the macabre.
results.correction_notes: Keep: the c05 crop-origin miracle after her death (c04), non-graphic. Closed eyes; no wounds, blood, gore or exposed body; a fully opaque robe; rice from both eyes and silkworms from her head; no Susanoo and no aura. Fix: (a) Make the miracle a powerful event, not a still life. Dense rice stalks surge up out of both eyes in two tall sheaves that rise high above her into the night. Heavy golden ears bend and shed grain that falls like rain onto the dark earth, and the soil around her stirs. Use a low, ground-level camera beside her head so the rice towers over the viewer, with one strong shaft of light on it. Optionally add the other non-graphic c05 origins (millet from the ears, azuki beans from the nose) as small, clear details. (b) Silkworms: a few unmistakable pale silkworm caterpillars emerging at the crown of her head, spinning fine glinting silk with a cocoon or two, so they read as silkworms being born. Not many grubs scattered across her hair and the soil. (c) Paint her in the house painterly style as an ancient Japanese goddess, in ancient-period layered robes (editorial) with serene, dignified features, not a photographic modern young woman. Reverent and majestic, never horror. No text.

results.reason: Viewed native 1254px, 200px, and hood, reaching-hand, wall-hand, key and foot/gate crops. One giant (ogre-de-la-caputxa-negra-c05/c06) with one head under a massive black hood. Inside the hood the face is fully covered by a draped black cloth veil, with no eyes, teeth or features showing (covered face, c01/c04). A plain iron key hangs on a chain at the centre of the chest (the key always worn at the neck, c03). Two arms: the near hand reaches straight at the viewer, thumb plus four thick fingers; the far hand grips the palace wall, showing three fingers and the thumb, with the fourth hidden. One huge boot strides forward onto the road; the other leg is under the cloak. The hands are charcoal-black, rough and leathery (Valencian ogres are black, c06) and read as monstrous skin, not a human ethnic caricature. A human-scale studded gate stands below his knee, so the giant scale is clear. It is the road outside his walled palace (c01/c05) at night under a full moon, which fits the sunlight weakness (c02/c05), and his step kicks up dust. No child, victim, gore, treasure, aura or text. The hood is the documented 'caputxa negra', and the huge leathery ogre hands and the striding giant keep it from copying any film wraith. The camera is at extreme low road level; at 200px the faceless giant reaching for the viewer is plainly terrifying.

Viewed native 1254px, 200px, and head/beak, both-foot, tail and spirit crops. One rooster (oilar-c01) with one head, one red serrated comb, red wattles, one visible eye (the other is on the hidden side) and one open pointed beak in full crow. Two wings are spread wide and there is one arched tail. Two legs: each foot grips the rock with its front toes and talons, and the hind toe and spur show on the shank. No extra legs, human face, horns or fangs. Four indistinct, smoky grey spirit shapes stream away from him toward the dark right side, their trailing wisps pointing back at him, so they read as fleeing his call (his crow announces the flight of spirits such as the lamiñak, c02). The receipt records that they are deliberately unspecified forms. A low sun breaks the horizon behind him while night still fills the sky (opening the day, c06), and it is the one dominant rim light. The extreme low camera on a rocky ridge lets the rooster fill the frame. No farmyard, people, text or aura. At 200px the crowing bird with spread wings driving off the ghostly shapes reads as a supernatural herald, not an ordinary farm rooster.
